**Ougi**: Increased damage. Further increased damage and damage cap when used against enemies with the Glaciate debuff.

Upon reaching Lv90, **Silverfrost Barrier** (skill 1) will be buffed, giving an additional buff to Water allies that reduces incoming Fire damage in conjunction with the buffed version of Lily's passive (to be described later).
In addition, when the enemy performs an Ougi, Lily will automatically cast **White Heal**, up to 3 times. 

Upon reaching Lv95, Lily's passive **"Shine Crystal"** will be buffed, giving +DEF to the entire team instead of just herself. In addition, incoming Fire damage is reduced against allies who have the new buff from Lily's improved Silverfrost Barrier. It is possible to give up to 5 stacks of this buff to each party member, and incoming Fire damage is reduced further for each stack.

Upon reaching Lv100, **Frozen Gale** (skill 2) will be buffed, adding a Stackable ATK+DEF down, and the CD will be reduced to 5 turns. In addition, the skill will be further buffed based on the number of different Races in the party (reminder, MC and Lily are both Unknowns, so they count as 1 Race). With *exactly* 2 races, the Damage Cap goes up, and with *3 or more* races, the ability will proc twice.

Also, Lily's 2nd passive, **"Envoy of the Crystalia"**, will be buffed to have maximum effectiveness with 3 Races on the team, instead of 4.

(someone please correct me if I'm incorrect on any of these details, thanks in advance!)

**Short answer:**

**Trial Deck recommendation order: Steins > Shiyoko > Yuuna >>>>> P5**

**Long-term completion recommendation order: Any one of those that isn't Shiyoko > Shiyoko**

For a player that is just starting out, Steins;Gate, Yuuna, or Shiyoko is the best **starting choice** due to their higher card quality. Steins and Yuuna are **Trial Deck+** as opposed to just Trial Deck, which means they have overall higher card quality, and none of the cards in the TD+ are 1-ofs. 

Shiyoko is a bit of a special case, since it is marketed as its own isolated deck. The deck is designed to have *extremely* generic cards, with generic (not BAD, but very generic) effects. Some of the standout cards of the Shiyoko deck include its Brainstorm Lv0, and its Level 3s. It is also a decent standalone deck.

Persona 5 TD is not a TD+ and doesn't get the same benefits as the ones I mentioned above. It will be quite weaker out of the box compared to the others.

As for **completed builds**, Shiyoko has very little for upgrades due to its nature as a standalone product. What little add-ons it has are all Promo cards, so you will have to hunt those down individually as, for the most part, they aren't mass-distributed.

Persona 5 is a pretty strong deck when completed, but it will use *almost none* of the cards from the Trial Deck (probably only like 2 cards).

Yuuna when completed is decently strong as well, and can make use of some of the cards from the TD+ such as the Lv3 Sagiri (secondary finisher), Lv3 Yuuna (healer), Lv2 Chitose support, Lv0 Chitose brainstorm, and Lv1 Yuuna Climax Combo.

Steins when completed is also a decent deck, and can also make use of some of the cards from the TD+. Some of the best cards from this TD+ include the Lv0 Kurisu (Runner), Lv0 Mayuri (Hand filter + Buffer), 3/2 Mayuri (Finisher), and 1/1 Event counter, and these are all options that can all be used in a completed build.

Most sets have different prices between the two languages, based on both the supply given to that language versus the demand of the community.

A perfect example of this is BanG Dream Girls Band Party. In Japanese, that set was printed to hell and back so there's a GIGANTIC supply of RRs available despite the high demand due to the popularity of the set. As a result, prices for RRs in this set (even the really good ones) are very low.

In English, Girls Band Party had a much smaller print run, causing cards such as Yukina Lv3 and Rimi Brainstorm to be much much more than their JP counterparts (for reference, Yukina Lv3 is like $12 in JP, but $30-40 in EN).

An opposite example would be Persona 5. In Japanese, cards such as Joker & Arsene Lv3 or the Protagonist Brainstorm are higher than in EN (Joker & Arsene is like $60 in JP while it's $35 in EN).

Between the booster set, TD, and promo, they have [14 cards](https://puu.sh/Dj8M4/112319b5a1.png) - 11 characters, 1 event, and 2 Climaxes. It's TECHNICALLY event to be a standalone deck, HOWEVER I would not put it as anywhere near good. I'd argue it's weaker than a Trial Deck+.

You do get to play a really solid brainstorm and combo it with 1/0 to potentially early summon 3/2 Kurousagis at Lv2 and then hopefully go from there. That's about your best play in the deck. You can't retain board at Lv0, you don't have a Lv1 CX combo to gain advantage off of, and your only other sources of cards are brainstorms (luck-reliant) or the 0/0 You (clocks you, and is also luck-reliant).

[Here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y0E4ffnkpc4) is footage from the World Championship Grand Finals played between the Japanese SAO player (and 2018 World Champion) Gaara, and the Hong Kong P5 player Lee Chun Fung. If you have the time to sit down and watch it, I highly recommend checking it out.

Lee Chun Fung's P5 build uses 1/0 Marker Protags as big costless 7k walls and 2/1 Protag Climax Combo as his early-mid game advantage engine. In the late game, he uses 3/2 Ryuji's Climax Combo to bounce opposing characters back to hand, completely eliminating the need to reverse of the opponent's characters in order to activate 3/2 Joker's finisher ability. In matchups where the opposing player has defensive counters (anti-damage counters, etc.) you can render those completely useless since you just remove all of their characters from the board, so you are doing direct attacks instead of front attacks.

IMO this is the optimal build of Persona 5.

EDIT: [This is Lee Chun Fung's deck list](https://scontent-sjc3-1.xx.fbcdn.net/v/t1.15752-9/50522240_595556364208368_5927658289910251520_n.png?_nc_cat=100&_nc_ht=scontent-sjc3-1.xx&oh=4eef1fd431dc618eb15eb255434e8598&oe=5D71A9B6).
